name: SELENE (Kaguya)
description: Japan's largest lunar mission since the Apollo era, this orbiter spent nearly two years mapping the Moon's gravity field and surface topography before a planned impact in 2009.

name: Akatsuki
description: A Venus climate orbiter built to study the planet's thick atmosphere and hunt for active volcanism, after an early engine failure delayed orbital insertion by five years.

name: QZS-1 (Michibiki)
description: The first satellite in Japan's Quasi-Zenith Satellite System, designed to improve GPS accuracy over Japan and the Asia-Oceania region from a high-inclination orbit.

name: GPM Core Observatory
description: A joint JAXA-NASA satellite carrying advanced radar and microwave instruments to set a new standard for measuring rain and snowfall from space worldwide.

name: ALOS-2 (Daichi-2)
description: A radar Earth-observation satellite used for disaster monitoring, forest mapping, and infrastructure surveillance regardless of weather or daylight conditions.

name: HTV-1 (Kounotori)
description: The debut flight of Japan's H-II Transfer Vehicle, an uncrewed cargo craft that went on to resupply the International Space Station for over a decade.

name: HTV-2 (Kounotori 2)
description: The second operational HTV cargo run, delivering food, spare parts, and science hardware to the International Space Station's Japanese Kibo module.

name: HTV-3 (Kounotori 3)
description: The third Kounotori resupply mission, carrying pressurized and unpressurized cargo to the space station aboard JAXA's heavier-lift H-IIB rocket.
